headline: Blues condemn 'vile messages of hate' by fans at recent home game
take:
ESPN reports that the St. Louis Blues condemned what the team called an antisemitic protest during a game last week at their home arena, describing the signs as "vile messages of hate." The report gives no further detail on who was involved or what comes next.

This is a story about conduct in the stands, and nothing in our numbers speaks to it. On the ice, STL sits at 5-5-1 for 11 points through 11 games, and the underlying play matches that middling record. The Blues have controlled 49.9% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality, so it tracks who generated the better looks) so far this season, essentially an even split. Their results have run slightly ahead of their chances, with 1.9 more goals than expected, while goaltending has given back 1.8 goals below expected. Those two roughly cancel, which fits a team that is .500 and playing like it. The sample is small, so we'd treat all of this as a snapshot, not a verdict.
